passages.original: Cujus tenorem VIA VENERABILIS PROSPER se cutus, hisdem Chronicis, hæc eadem egregia brevitate composuit, ut eorum initium a mundi inchoaretur exordio. Hæc Victorius Aquitanus, qui hoc in arauo opere non alios seculus esse declarat ducet quam Eusebium, Hieronymum ac Prosperum, quem sanctum ac venerabilem, tum venerabilem virum appellat, qua vol simili nuncupatione designatur Aquitanus noster apud antiquos: ne quis alium a populari suo indigitare voluisse Victorium suspicetur...
passages.english: Following its course, the venerable man Prosper composed these same things in the same Chronicle with remarkable brevity, so that its beginning started from the very origin of the world. So says Victorius of Aquitaine, who declares that in this arduous work he followed no other guides than Eusebius, Jerome and Prosper, whom he calls holy and venerable, and again a venerable man, the title, or one like it, by which our Aquitanian is designated among the ancients, so that no one should suspect that Victorius meant to point to anyone other than his fellow countryman...
passages.notes: Several scanning errors read as intended: 'VIA VENERABILIS' as 'vir venerabilis', 'se cutus' as 'secutus', 'arauo' as 'arduo', 'seculus' as 'secutus', 'ducet' as 'duces', 'vol' as 'vel'. 'hisdem Chronicis' is taken as 'in the same Chronicle' (i.e., continuing Eusebius' chronicle). The passage breaks off with an ellipsis in the source.
